en.title: ECB keeps key interest rate at 2.5%
en.dek: On 29 October 2026 the ECB left its key rate at 2.5% and President Christine Lagarde announced she will step down on 7 February 2027.
facts: ECB kept its main policy rate at 2.5% on 29 Oct 2026 (Tagesschau, CNBC).
Christine Lagarde announced she will resign effective 7 Feb 2027 (Euronews, The Straits Times).
Lagarde said the Governing Council debated a hike and a December move is now in focus (Euronews, Morningstar).
The ECB cited an energy shock as a driver of inflation (Morningstar).
The euro rose against the dollar after the decision (CNA).
European equities rose in Thursday trading after the decision (Yahoo Finance).
body: The European Central Bank kept its main policy rate at 2.5% on 29 October 2026, according to Tagesschau.
CNBC reported the same decision, confirming the rate was left unchanged.
Christine Lagarde announced she will resign as ECB president effective 7 February 2027, Euronews reported.
The Straits Times also stated the resignation date.
Lagarde said she wants freedom to speak on topics beyond monetary policy, as quoted by France 24.
The Governing Council debated a possible rate hike, Lagarde said, according to Euronews.
Morningstar noted that a December move is now in focus for the council.
The post‑meeting statement cited an energy shock as a driver of inflation, Morningstar reported.
It linked the shock to persistent price pressures above target.
The euro edged higher against the dollar after the decision, CNA reported.
Yahoo Finance said European equities rose in Thursday trading following the announcement.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the EU is exploring associate membership for Canada, the South China Morning Post reported.
The Straits Times noted the proposal is divisive among member states.
en.context: Morningstar reported that the ECB said an energy shock kept inflation above its 2 % target, prompting the rate hold. CNBC noted the bank’s main refinancing rate guides borrowing costs across the euro area.

en.dek: On 29 October 2026 the ECB left its key rate at 2.5% and President Christine Lagarde announced she will step down on 7 February 2027.
body: Lagarde announced she will step down on 7 February 2027, according to Euronews and The Straits Times. She said she wants freedom to speak on topics beyond monetary policy, reported by The Straits Times and France 24.

The ECB held its main policy rate at 2.5% on 29 October 2026, according to Tagesschau and CNBC. Yahoo Finance and CNA also reported the decision was made on Thursday. The decision left the rate unchanged, maintaining the 2.5% level set earlier this year.

Lagarde told the Governing Council that members debated a possible hike and that a December move is now in focus, as reported by Euronews. Morningstar noted the December hike moved into focus following the meeting, indicating policymakers may act if inflation persists.
The ECB cited an energy shock as a driver of inflation when it left rates unchanged, according to Morningstar. The agency linked the shock to persistent price pressures that remain above target.
The euro edged higher against the dollar after the decision, reported by CNA. Yahoo Finance said European equities rose in Thursday trading following the announcement.
Lagarde’s early exit comes months before the end of her mandate, as noted by The Straits Times. Bloomberg described her step down as occurring amid growing economic pressure.

Lagarde announced resignation effective 7 Feb 2027 (Euronews, The Straits Times).

ECB cited an energy shock as an inflation driver (Morningstar).

de.dek: Am 29. Oktober 2026 beließ die EZB ihren Leitzins bei 2,5 %, und Präsidentin Christine Lagarde kündigte an, am 7. Februar 2027 zurückzutreten.
body: Lagarde kündigte an, dass sie am 7. Februar 2027 zurücktreten wird, so Euronews und The Straits Times. Sie erklärte, sie wünsche sich die Freiheit, über Themen jenseits der Geldpolitik zu sprechen, berichteten The Straits Times und France 24.

Die EZB beließ ihren Leitzins am 29. Oktober 2026 bei 2,5 %, laut Tagesschau und CNBC. Yahoo Finance und CNA berichteten ebenfalls, dass die Entscheidung am Donnerstag getroffen wurde. Die Entscheidung ließ den Zinssatz unverändert und hielt das Anfang des Jahres festgelegte Niveau von 2,5 % bei.

Lagarde teilte dem Rat mit, dass die Mitglieder über eine mögliche Erhöhung debattiert hätten und dass ein Schritt im Dezember nun im Fokus stehe, wie Euronews berichtete. Morningstar merkte an, dass die Dezember-Erhöhung nach dem Treffen in den Fokus rückte, was darauf hindeutet, dass die Entscheidungsträger handeln könnten, falls die Inflation anhält.

Die EZB nannte einen Energieschock als Treiber der Inflation, als sie die Zinsen unverändert ließ, so Morningstar. Die Agentur verknüpfte den Schock mit anhaltendem Preisdruck, der über dem Zielwert bleibt.
Der Euro legte nach der Entscheidung gegenüber dem Dollar leicht zu, berichtete CNA. Yahoo Finance gab an, dass europäische Aktien im Donnerstagshandel nach der Ankündigung stiegen.

Lagardes vorzeitiger Abschied erfolgt Monate vor dem Ende ihres Mandats, wie The Straits Times anmerkte. Bloomberg beschrieb ihren Rücktritt als eine Entscheidung inmitten wachsenden wirtschaftlichen Drucks.

The rate decision was reported by Tagesschau and CNBC, which both said the ECB held the rate at 2.5%.
Lagarde said the ECB debated a rate hike and hinted at a possible move in December. Euronews reported that she made the statement, and Morningstar noted that the December hike is now in focus.
Lagarde confirmed her resignation in a statement released by The Straits Times and CNBC. She said she would step down before the end of her term to speak freely on topics beyond monetary policy.
The ECB cited an energy shock as a driver of inflation when it left rates unchanged. Morningstar reported that the energy shock is an inflation driver.
The decision comes after months of speculation about Lagarde’s future. The Straits Times reported that her resignation is effective 7 February 2027.
